- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent peak or use 20-day moving average as ceiling.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model frequently underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias: if price is above 20-day MA by >3%, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture late-stage momentum; if sentiment turns bullish after day 15, increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day for final 5 days.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model tends to average out; use sentiment-weighted median of recent 5-day highs/lows to adjust forecast midpoint.
